# A bill posted to an account declared `type: Liability`, not Accounts Payable.
#
# GnuCash's engine does not check it. `gncInvoicePostToAccount` validates
# nothing about the account it is handed, and this tool's own posting check
# compares currencies only — so `ap_account:` naming a plain liability is a
# book that gets built, and the bill posts to it.
#
# It exists to separate two questions that usually have the same answer:
# whether a record is a bill (its owner is a vendor) and whether the account
# it posted to is of type Accounts Payable. Here the first is true and the
# second is false, so anything deciding "bill or invoice" from the account's
# type gets it wrong while everything deciding from the owner gets it right —
# and a refusal built from both says "this bill's own receivable".
#
# What this fixture produces: a posted bill owing 100.00 USD whose payable is
# `Liabilities:Other Payables`, declared a plain liability.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
2026-01-01 commodity FUNDX
	mnemonic: "FUNDX"
	fullname: "Example Balanced Fund"
	namespace: "FUND"
	fraction: 100
2026-01-01 open Liabilities:Other Payables
	type: Liability
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Fund
	type: Mutual Fund
	commodity.namespace: "FUND"
	commodity.mnemonic: "FUNDX"
	commodity_scu: 1000
2026-03-30 * "Bill on a plain liability, settled in units"
	guid: "2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0c5f6a7b8c9d0e1f"
	currency.mnemonic: "USD"
	Assets:Bank:USD -100.00 USD
		guid: "3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0c5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a"
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
	Assets:Fund 1.000 FUNDX
		guid: "4c5d6e7f8a9b0c5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b"
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "FUNDX"
		share_price: "100"
		value: "100.00"
